images.title: Two moves to the alternate angle
images.purpose: Show f reaching d by a corresponding move then a vertically opposite move.
images.composition: Two parallel lines and a transversal in the centre; two curved arrows and three coloured angles, nothing else.
exact_structure: Two horizontal parallel lines, l above and m below, each with two small arrow marks (>>) at the right end.
A transversal t that goes up to the left and down to the right, crossing l and m.
Angle f: upper right angle at the crossing with m, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled f = 120°.
Angle b: upper right angle at the crossing with l, filled amber (#E69F00), labelled b = 120°.
Angle d: lower left angle at the crossing with l, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled d = 120°.
A grey (#6B7280) arrow up along t from f to b, labelled Move 1.
A grey (#6B7280) curved arrow across the crossing with l from b to d, labelled Move 2.
All other angles are drawn with no fill and no label.
rejection: a different angle from f, b, d filled
any value other than 120° on f, b or d
missing arrow marks on the lines
images.takeaway: f to b to d: two moves keep the size, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal.
images.description: Parallel lines with angles f, b and d each 120°, joined by arrows labelled Move 1 and Move 2.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students trace the two arrows from f to d.

image_decisions.why: The two-move path is the reason alternate angles match.
